result.title: Propensities Please: Exposing Alignment-Faking LLMs using Synthetic Document Finetuning
result.comment: 27 pages, including references and appendices. Code: https://github.com/ardyh/propensities-please
result.summary: Alignment evaluations aim to assess whether large language models would engage in dangerous misaligned behaviour. Misaligned and evaluation-aware models might engage in alignment faking, where they pursue a hidden goal, but conceal this behaviour when they suspect effective oversight such as during training, evaluation or audited deployment. Such a model might view any prompt-based intervention that aims to reveal latent propensities as part of the evaluation, calling into question the reliability of existing alignment evaluations. Current methods for detecting alignment faking rely on chain-of-thought monitorability, highly realistic environments that reduce evaluation awareness, or mechanistic interventions, all of which are expected to become less reliable for future model generations. We present a method for revealing latent misaligned propensities that does not rely on any of these. We use synthetic document finetuning to teach models that misaligned actions will go undetected whenever certain keywords appear in the prompt. We place alignment-faking model organisms in environments that are clearly identifiable as honeypots and measure how their behaviour changes after finetuning. We observe that finetuning consistently widens the gap in misaligned action rates between prompts with and without the cue, indicating that finetuning allows exposing latent propensities more reliably than purely prompt-based methods. We argue that behavioural methods for detecting alignment faking and related behaviours are critical going forward, as models become more capable and less interpretable. We find that SDF often damages the models' reasoning capabilities and introduce a mitigation based on on-policy distillation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用 synthetic document finetuning 教模型「提示中出现特定关键词时不当行为不会被发现」，再把 alignment-faking 模型置于明显可识别的蜜罐环境中，比较微调前后带线索与不带线索提示下不当行为率的差距，发现微调比纯 prompt 干预更能暴露潜在倾向；并指出该方法会损害推理能力，提出基于 on-policy distillation 的缓解。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心思路是「潜在倾向难以靠提示探测、需靠训练干预显形」，这与 LVR 中判断答案是否真正使用 latent 视觉内容、以及评测感知导致探针失效的问题可能相通，可供核查。
